core_obligations: Divisibility of injective sheaves (proof lines 4226-4232): an injective abelian sheaf is divisible, since a local section is a map from the sheaf represented by the object and injectivity applies to multiplication by an integer.

Torsion subcomplexes of injective complexes (proof lines 4233-4264): for a complex of injective abelian sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are torsion, the inclusion of the torsion subcomplex is a quasi-isomorphism; this uses flatness of the rationals over the integers for the tensor product and divisibility for the lifting of sections.

K-injectivity and the adjunction (proof lines 4265-4278): the displayed identification of homotopy classes of maps into the torsion subcomplex shows that it is K-injective whenever the ambient complex is, and the resulting identities on the derived categories show that the inclusion of the derived category of torsion sheaves is an equivalence onto the complexes whose cohomology is torsion, by the adjoint criterion.
proof_roadmap: Observe that injective abelian sheaves are divisible.
Show that the torsion subcomplex of a complex of injectives with torsion cohomology is a quasi-isomorphism.
Deduce K-injectivity and conclude with the criterion for adjoint functors.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the derived category of the Serre subcategory of torsion abelian sheaves with the complexes on the site whose cohomology sheaves are torsion (statement lines 4217-4223). The proof is a complete chain of homological algebra: injective abelian sheaves are shown to be divisible (proof lines 4226-4232); a comparison of the torsion subcomplex of a complex of injective sheaves with torsion cohomology with the complex itself is proved to be a quasi-isomorphism using flatness of the rationals and divisibility (proof lines 4233-4264); and the homotopy classes of maps into the torsion subcomplex are identified so that it is K-injective, after which the adjoint criterion gives the equivalence (proof lines 4265-4278). The non-formal content is the identification of the derived categories. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each algebraic input named.
